text_copy: AUDIT/primary/jaramillo-mazo2026-cacao-cd-bacteria.txt (copy of Marker markdown; no PDF in library)
disposition_reason: Soil microbiology study: 16S rDNA sequencing of 225 rhizosphere soils from 5 cacao farms (Antioquia and Santander, Colombia, 2020 and 2022) and isothermal microcalorimetry with 1 mg/L CdCl2 spiking. It reports soil Cd categories and bacterial taxa responses only; no bean, nib or product Cd values and no tested intervention with a bean-Cd outcome. Authors state microbial communities alone are unlikely to remove Cd from soils.
disposition_locator: Abstract; Methods 'Soil sampling'; Results 'Soil core bacteria across different soil Cd categories'; Discussion 'Bacteria responded to Cd spiked in experimental conditions'

study.design: farm survey (soil microbiome) plus laboratory microcalorimetry assay
study.material_scope: rhizosphere soil (0-20 cm) under cacao; no beans analysed in this paper
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Colombia: Antioquia (Uraba and Magdalena subregions) and Santander (San Vicente de Chucuri); not a market study
study.sampling_unit: composite rhizosphere soil per plant (3 subsamples); 16 plots, 5 farms; IMC on 60 samples
study.method: 16S rDNA V3-V4 Illumina MiSeq; isothermal microcalorimetry (TAM Air, 80 h, 25 C) with 1 mg/L CdCl2; soil Cd method not described in this paper (refers to companion study [12])
study.basis: soil, air-dried (Cd fraction, total vs available, not stated)

controls.control: Soil bacterial community (Cd-tolerant taxa such as Flavobacterium, Novosphingobium, Lysobacter, Rhizobium, Caulobacter) as a possible bioremediation/bioaugmentation lever
controls.design: observational soil survey and in-vitro calorimetry
controls.comparator: low soil Cd (0-1 mg/kg) vs high soil Cd (2-4.3 mg/kg) categories; spiked vs unspiked soil aliquots
controls.outcome: About 28% of community responded to high soil Cd (13% increased, 15% decreased in differential abundance); 27% of taxa changed during IMC. No bean Cd outcome measured; authors note microbes 'alone are unlikely to directly remove Cd contamination from soils'.
controls.locator: Results 'Soil core bacteria...'; Discussion 'Bacteria responded to Cd spiked...'

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary says 'PERMANOVA p < 0.001 for both' farm and Cd; primary reports CAP p<0.001, PERMANOVA Cd/FARM p<0.05 and Cd/PLOT p<0.001.
Stored summary labels soil Cd as 'DTPA-extractable or total'; the primary does not state which fraction.

Stored summary presents genera as 'candidates for bioaugmentation strategies'; the primary is more cautious, stating microbial communities alone are unlikely to remove Cd and suggesting possible indirect roles.
Stored summary says '28% of phyla responded'; primary says 46 phyla identified, 'of which 28% correspond to taxa that respond' (unit of the percentage ambiguous).
unresolved: Soil Cd analytical method and fraction are deferred to companion study [12] (Jaramillo-Mazo et al., bean Cd and translocation); bean Cd values for these farms would need that paper.
Primary read from Marker markdown conversion; no PDF available to cross-check figures and supplementary tables (S1-S3).
